messages:
Anika: Heads-up — replaying tenant-42 snapshot and integrity check failed. manifest sha256 != computed tarball sha256 :rotating_light:
Mike: Ugh. Which fields differ?
Anika: manifest in snapshots/tenant42/2026-03-20/manifest.json lists `sha256: 3b7f...ea9c` but local compute is `a9d2...1f33`. Downloaded directly from backups-prod bucket.
Sara: Any chance it's a streaming chunk reorder or partial upload?
Anika: I thought that — but file sizes match and gzip header looks sane. Quick verify command I ran:
```
sha256sum tenant42-2026-03-20.tar.gz
# -> a9d2...1f33  tenant42-2026-03-20.tar.gz
```
Mike: Can you paste the S3 metadata? maybe we re-encrypted and lost x-amz-meta-sha256 or CMK changed.
Anika: Head-object metadata shows `x-amz-meta-sha256: 3b7f...ea9c` and `x-amz-meta-cmk-id: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/old-cmk`. But object was re-encrypted during lifecycle job on 2026-03-21.
Javier: So metadata SHA says one value but object content is different — suggests the lifecycle re-encrypt job replaced object bytes without preserving metadata or there was a partial copy. Which uploader path wrote the manifest?
Anika: Manifest created by backup-uploader v1.9 during snapshot creation (pre-lifecycle). Lifecycle copy job is encryptor-daemon v2.2 which ran later and performs S3 CopyObject with SSE-KMS. I suspect CopyObject didn't set `MetadataDirective: REPLACE` correctly or it did replace and used stale metadata.
Sara: If CopyObject used REPLACE but didn't copy the original x-amz-meta-sha256, manifest will disagree. Two possibilities: encryptor mutated object (bad) or uploader generated manifest for a different tarball (weird).
encops-bot: Automated alert: snapshot-integrity-check failed for tenant-42 (snapshot id: snap-20260320-42). Investigating queue created: ENCOPS-4321.
Mike: Action items: (1) Stop lifecycle re-encrypt for tenant-42 prefix (put a temporary lifecycle pause), (2) fetch original object version from versioning if available, (3) run aws s3api head-object to compare ETag/Metadata and copy-source-version-id.
Anika: I ran the head-object and also downloaded object via `aws s3 cp s3://backups-prod/snapshots/tenant42/2026-03-20/tenant42-2026-03-20.tar.gz .` The ETag and Content-Length match what uploader reported. Versioning is enabled — I'm grabbing prior version now.
Javier: If prior version has correct sha256 we can reconcile by updating manifest or restoring the correct artifact and then rotate CMK. If prior version is also bad, escalate to infra for possible uploader bug.
Sara: Also check KMS decrypt logs — maybe decrypt+re-encrypt changed bytes if SSE-C vs SSE-KMS mismatch. Run: 
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket backups-prod --key snapshots/tenant42/2026-03-20/tenant42-2026-03-20.tar.gz --query '{Metadata:Metadata,ETag:ETag,VersionId:VersionId}'
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/backup-encrypt-key
```
Mike: Assigning: Anika to fetch prior version and checksum (ETA 30m). Javier to check encryptor-daemon copy logic and recent deploys. Sara to review KMS grant changes in last 48h. I'll open an incident if we don't have a clean prior artifact.
Anika: Got prior version (versionId: v-0a1b2c). Its sha256 matches manifest (3b7f...ea9c). So current head is a later copy that lost metadata but changed bytes. I've paused lifecycle for tenant42 prefix.
encops-bot: ENCOPS-4321 updated: lifecycle paused for s3://backups-prod/snapshots/tenant42/ (by Anika).
Mike: Good. Next steps: (a) restore the prior version to replace the bad one (use CopyObject with MetadataDirective=COPY to preserve metadata), (b) run a small end-to-end restore test, (c) add a safeguard in encryptor-daemon to preserve x-amz-meta-sha256 and emit a post-copy verification step.
Javier: I found a regression in encryptor-daemon v2.2 — a change to use `REPLACE` but metadata map was set to empty when CMK rotation path hit. I'll ship a small hotfix to set MetadataDirective=COPY when sha metadata exists. PR coming in ~20m.
Sara: I'll check CloudTrail KMS events for any grant/rotate operations 48h window and add notes to ENCOPS-4321.
Anika: I'll restore prior version and run checksum validation and then kick an automated replay smoke test.
Mike: Thanks. Keep updates on ENCOPS-4321. If anyone hits surprises ping me directly. :thumbsup:
